title: fserv bot (RRC channel)
summary: mIRC-style fserv bot that answers triggers in the RRC channel. Ships base templates and an editable dialogue table.

activation.note: The only change to any Stump file. Natural home is example_node.py, after RRC exists and before the server starts serving.
activation.removal: Delete the two lines and the fservbot/ folder.

wizard.note: Only the password prompt matters. If the technician leaves it blank, the bot still runs and still answers its base triggers -- only editing is off. Everything else can be set later from the RRC channel by a user who has the password.

prompts.prompt: fserv bot operator password (blank = dialogue editing off)
prompts.help: Anyone in the RRC channel who knows this can add/remove the bot's dialogues with /fsadd and /fsdel. Blank means nobody can, including the technician, until it is set. It travels as plain chat over plain HTTP -- a deterrent, not a security boundary.

prompts.prompt: Trigger character the bot answers to
prompts.help: Single character, must not be '/' (that is RRC's own command prefix). Changeable later from chat with /fsset. Skip this prompt unless the room already uses '!' for something else.

prompts.prompt: Minutes between 'what I am' notices in the channel (0 = off)
prompts.help: The classic fserv channel ad. Posted on chat activity, never to an empty room, and never more often than this. Minimum 5 when enabled. Changeable later with /fsset.

config_block: # Blank password = dialogue editing is OFF. The bot still answers its
# base triggers; only /fsadd and /fsdel are refused. Set this to let a
# user in the RRC channel configure the bot after boot.

runtime_storage.note: Dialogues and runtime options. Created on first edit. No SD card means edits last until reboot; the bot says so when it saves. Delete this file to return to shipped defaults.

user_commands.note: Available in the RRC channel after boot. Password-gated commands are marked.

manifest_note: provisioner.py's EXPECTED_FILE_HASHES needs one entry per file above. No existing entry changes: this plugin edits no file it did not create. plugin.json and README.md are documentation and may be excluded from the upload set if the team prefers to keep the 52-file payload lean -- core.py, templates.py, install.py and __init__.py are the only files needed at runtime.
